elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Rendered clause 7.7 reads in full: "Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement." The 15%-of-annual-Fees-per-week formula is deleted in its entirety, leaving no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic, and the prohibition is unconditional and Agreement-wide.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no Customer-payable liquidated amount of any kind (clause 7.7 now bars all liquidated damages and penalties; § 10 imposes no termination fee and § 27 permits termination "without penalty"), so the restriction on the character of any such amount is vacuously satisfied.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no early-termination fee is imposed anywhere in the retained or rendered text, so there is no amount requiring a three-month cap. The preferred outcome (zero) is not exceeded by any capped figure.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with clause 7.7 replaced by a blanket bar, no liquidated amount is payable by Customer at all, so exclusivity of an early-termination fee is vacuously satisfied.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: the single element is met by an unconditional, operative prohibition ("Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages or penalties under this Agreement"), with the punitive 15%/week formula fully excised rather than merely capped or narrowed.

Fallback elements are conditional on the existence of a Customer-payable liquidated amount; because the redline eliminates all such amounts and no early-termination fee exists in § 10 or § 27, those conditions do not arise and the fallback is not contradicted.

Minimal: the edit is confined to the single sentence constituting the target liquidated damages mechanic. Nothing outside clause 7.7 is touched, no survival tail, expense language, procedure, or additional remedy is added, and no operative term is duplicated.

Preserves intent: Vendor's § 7.3 late-payment and general remedies for genuine non-payment survive untouched, payment timing and invoicing mechanics are unaffected, and the replacement sentence leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference (the now-unused reliance on the "annual Fees" measure disappears with the deleted formula, which is helpful given "Fees" is defined only as the Implementation Fee).

Finding status "deviation" is correct: the original clause was walk-away territory — a liquidated sum triggered by a minor breach (payment ten days late) that compounds weekly and can exceed the remaining contract value — so it fails the fallback on material terms rather than being a minor sub-element shortfall.
